reviews.text:
I just got out of an abusive marriage, looking to restore my faith in people. Bumble seemed cute and friendly. I mistakenly purchased premium services, holy moly, what a waste. 

To be clear, I’m not unattractive, good shape, educated, employed, have an adorable dog and a winning sense of humor. These services rendered little observable benefit, so I suspended my account to pursue other avenues.

Then I got hit with the $180 renewal, eeek. Okay, fair, I mistakenly forgot to turn off auto renewal, I own that.

Here’s where things get interesting, I reached out to customer service, see if they can help out seeing as it’s obvious I have not been using it, as expected, cold and heartless… they’re hands are tied. Fine, I get that.

Here’s where things get shady. So as part of the premium services you are supposed to get x number of perks per week. But although you have pre-paid for the perks, you cannot keep them, they reset every week, do not accumulate.

So not only was I hit with the renewal to a service that is ‘meh’ to begin with, I essentially have nothing to show for it.

I was totally planning on unleashing all those accumulated perks to make a real push… alas, surprise, surprise … MONEY IN… ACCOUNTABILITY OFF.

Anywho, not my proudest moment, but at least the lesson is painful enough to last.

The algorithm feels heavily biased, with virtually no transparency about how profiles are displayed, prioritized, or whether paying customers receive meaningful exposure. Bumble continues to push premium subscriptions and additional purchases without delivering noticeable improvements in results.

reviews.title: Ich kann Bumble nach meinen Erfahrungen nicht empfehlen.
reviews.text:
Mein Konto wurde ohne für mich nachvollziehbaren Grund gesperrt. Auf meinen Einspruch hin wurde die Sperrung bestätigt. Eine konkrete Begründung, welcher Verstoß mir überhaupt vorgeworfen wird, habe ich trotz Nachfrage nicht erhalten. Stattdessen gab es lediglich eine allgemeine Standardantwort, dass die Entscheidung endgültig sei.

Was mich besonders ärgert: Nutzer können offenbar sehr einfach andere Profile melden. Wenn es jedoch um eine Kontosperrung geht, fehlt es aus meiner Sicht an Transparenz und einer nachvollziehbaren Überprüfung. Als betroffener Nutzer hat man kaum eine Möglichkeit, sich gegen eine solche Entscheidung zu wehren oder überhaupt zu erfahren, was man falsch gemacht haben soll.

Ich habe Bumble respektvoll genutzt und kann bis heute keinen Grund erkennen, der eine dauerhafte Sperrung rechtfertigen würde. Dass eine solche Entscheidung getroffen wird, ohne den Betroffenen konkret über den Vorwurf zu informieren, halte ich für inakzeptabel.

Ein Dating-Portal sollte nicht nur Wert auf möglichst einfache Meldefunktionen legen, sondern auch auf faire Verfahren, nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen und einen erreichbaren Kundenservice. Genau das habe ich hier vermisst.

Für mich ist Bumble damit erledigt. Ein Stern ist noch zu viel.

So, it doesn’t let me set a new first photo that it doesn’t believe meets this criteria - pretty annoying!

That said, I have been disappointed with this app in general lately, though I’ve enjoyed it a lot in the past. If nothing else, it seems that Bumble’s user base has really fallen off. I redownloaded Bumble a few months ago after about a year and a half of not using it, and I run out of potential matches much faster than I used to, despite being in the same city and now being at an age more generally sought after than before. I also notice small visual glitches with the app quite frequently.

It’s a shame, as in the past I’ve had nice successes meeting people via Bumble. I’ve had some success with actual dates since redownloading, but Hinge and even Tinder just do the job much better nowadays (not something I would have said before my 1.5 year break from dating apps).

reviews.text:
Es ist schon auffällig: Aktivierst du am letzten Tag dein Spotlight, bekommst du plötzlich ein Like. Doch sobald das Spotlight abgelaufen ist, kannst du dir dieses Like nicht mehr anschauen. Zufall? Schwer zu glauben.

Man bekommt zunehmend das Gefühl, dass hier gezielt mit der Neugier und Hoffnung der Nutzer gespielt wird, um sie dazu zu bringen, erneut Geld zu investieren.

Spotlight läuft, Like kommt. Spotlight vorbei, Like nicht mehr sichtbar. Abo abgelaufen, plötzlich neue Likes.

Das wirkt alles andere als vertrauenswürdig. Ob das tatsächlich Absicht ist, kann ich nicht beweisen, aber als Nutzer fühlt man sich regelrecht zum Bezahlen gedrängt.

Bumble sollte sich darauf konzentrieren, echte Kontakte zu ermöglichen, statt den Eindruck zu vermitteln, dass Likes und Matches vor allem dazu dienen, Nutzer zum Abschluss eines kostenpflichtigen Abos zu bewegen.

I use Bumble because I want to support the female leadership behind it.
However, the app tends to send unintentional likes and super-likes to people I am pretty sure I did not intend to swipe right on.
It also hides the revert button for “given” likes including those unintentional likes.
This way I am losing my limited super-likes, also giving false hope to others. My unintentional like might cause people to pay Bumble for unlocking the visibility of their received likes, and then get disappointed when they find out it was unintentional or feel rejected by getting unmatched instantly after a match.
This might generate more income for Bumble, but does hiding the revert button really align with Bumble’s core values?  Especially considering Bumble was started after the company’s history with Tinder? The CEO left Tinder to make a difference but now indirectly giving false hope to people (including women)?

I used Bumble for about a month and initially had very good results. Then I met a woman who behaved very rudely. Since I had not ordered or drunk anything, I did not feel responsible for paying for the cocktail she chose to have.

I politely told her that I did not feel a connection and preferred not to continue the date. Shortly afterward, my account was permanently banned. I strongly suspect that she reported me in retaliation, although Bumble never provided any specific evidence or explanation.

Bumble knows this and every 4-5 likes will send a pop up that says “second time is a charm! Pay more money to send a compliment so these girls that we know are a good match for you will notice you”. Sorry, I paid for premium and you want me to pay AGAIN so a girl I liked will see my like?? You really want to hide my like from a girl that will be a good match until I pay a second time? This is an awful business strategy. I get that the goal of the app is to make money, but forcing a premium user to make a second payment just to get a match is diabolical. It’s pretty obvious that if I swipe on a match that seems an okay match for me, bumble will give me that match, but if I swipe on a match that is a great match for me, bumble refuses to give me that match unless I pay again. Disgusting business practices! Fellas avoid this app and do not pay any of your hard earned money

Je mag alles zelf doen: al je privégegevens invoeren, zoeken, keuren, scannen en hopen dat er iets tussen zit wat je mee naar huis wilt nemen.

Ook blijkt een aantrekkelijk artikel bij nader inzien regelmatig toch niet beschikbaar, krijg je geen enkele reactie of verdwijnt het spontaan uit je mandje.

Ondertussen blijf je braaf doorscannen, tot je je begint af te vragen waarom je hier eigenlijk zoveel tijd aan besteedt. En ja: ik heb een eerlijk profiel met vlot leesbare teksten en leuke, onbewerkte foto’s van mezelf geplaatst, dus daar kan het onmogelijk aan liggen. 😉

Het verschil met de zelfscankassa: daar betaal ik voor iets wat ik daadwerkelijk mee naar huis neem. Bij Bumble moet ik betalen om een foutje te herstellen en daarna maar afwachten of er überhaupt iets van die match terechtkomt.

reviews.text:
I am very disappointed with my experience with Bumble Support.

I contacted support to restore my deleted account and provided my ID as requested. There were delays in the communication, and the restoration process involved several rounds of emails over a number of weeks.

The most frustrating part was that I later learned my account could no longer be restored because the 28-day period had expired. By the time I saw the final instructions and responded, the deadline had already passed. I understand that I was not able to reply before the deadline, but the overall communication process also felt slow and difficult to follow, especially for an issue where timing is so important.

I wish there had been a clearer warning that the restoration deadline was approaching or that an active support case would receive more timely handling. Losing my account and its data has been really upsetting.

I hope Bumble improves its communication and support process for users facing account restoration issues.

reviews.title: An absolute scam
reviews.text:
6’5 French/American guy, very athletic, MBA, educated, avid traveler, cultured, and a photographer to boot, so I know how to take good pictures. No gym shots, party shots, shots with other women, etc… (I have been told by strangers multiple times I look like Tom Cruise, Josh Brolin, and even Tom Brady among others. Not that looks are the only thing that matters, but those shouldn’t be responsible for my negative experience on this app). 
Six months on here and I’ve had maybe a GRAND TOTAL of three matches, resulting in one date (we went out together for a month before realizing our personalities weren’t compatible). 
Although I “swipe right” rather conservatively, I must have done so on at least an additional 90+ women by now. Odds are, at least one of those women would have “liked me back”, but no. Absolute crickets. It’s safe to assume that my profile is in no way shape or form visible to any potential matches due to whatever algorithm they employ. 
I did try the premium subscription in order to boost my visibility, but still nothing (so much so I demanded a refund which I never do on apps). 
This app is an absolute scam. They don’t care about helping you find a potential partner, but only about taking your money. reviews.title: Fatal
reviews.text:
Developers of apps like Hinge have indeed caused more harm than good. But the main problem isn’t even the apps themselves — it’s how women choose to use them.
They receive such an overwhelming amount of attention, likes, and offers that they’ve stopped taking people seriously. When there’s an endless stream of admirers, the attitude naturally becomes consumer-like.

In these apps, it’s women who make the final decisions: they choose whom to reply to, whom to ignore, whom to cancel on at the last minute, and whom to drop without explanation. And this is exactly why the current toxic dynamic exists — it’s a direct result of their behavior.
The issue isn’t the algorithm; it’s how women act when they have complete control over the situation.

The abundance of options makes their approach superficial: today they reply, tomorrow they ghost, the next day they ruin all plans without giving a second thought to the other person’s feelings or time.
Not because they lack manners, but because they know: “if anything goes wrong — I still have a hundred more options lined up.”

This creates a culture of irresponsibility.
And yes — the blame lies with women, because they’re the ones setting the rules of the game by using their advantage of choice.
